name: Thirumeninathar Temple, Tiruchuli (Thiruchuzhiyal)
deity: Shiva as Thirumeninathar (Bhoominathar), with the goddess Thunaimalai Nayaki
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Pandya Nadu, sung by Sundarar in the Tevaram (8th century)
summary: At Tiruchuli in Virudhunagar district, Shiva as Thirumeninathar is remembered as the Lord who stilled the great flood — a shrine sung by Sundarar, in the town where Ramana Maharshi was born.

sections.history: Tiruchuli is a small town of the dry southern plain, about 15 km east of Aruppukottai on the road towards Manamadurai. In the Tevaram it is Thiruchuzhiyal, and Sundarar sang a pathigam to its Lord that is gathered in the seventh Tirumurai, making the temple one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and one of the fourteen of Pandya Nadu. Tradition adds that the saint stayed in a monastery here. In modern times the town has drawn seekers for another reason: Ramana Maharshi was born here in 1879, and his family home, now the Sundara Mandiram, stands close to the temple.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian shrine of the Pandya country, with the sanctum of Thirumeninathar and a separate shrine for the goddess Thunaimalai Nayaki. A shrine of Pralaya Vidangar, the Lord who mastered the deluge, recalls the temple's founding story. Opposite the entrance lies the sacred tank called the Kavvaikadal, whose water rises and falls with the seasons of this rain-shadowed land.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of a great flood, a pralaya, that threatened to drown the world. Shiva drove his trident into the earth here, and the rushing waters drained away into the opening it made, so that the land was saved. For this the Lord is also called Pralaya Vidangar and Bhoominathar, protector of the earth. One telling links the deliverance to a Pandya king, Bruhat Balan, whom Shiva also freed from the sin of taking life.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri, Arudra Darshanam in Margazhi and the monthly Pradosham are kept with devotion, along with the temple's annual festival. Ramana Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Ramana Maharshi, draws visitors to the Sundara Mandiram around December–January; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Tiruchuli is unhurried, and a visit can join two kinds of pilgrimage. Worship Thirumeninathar and the goddess Thunaimalai Nayaki, look out over the Kavvaikadal tank, then walk the short way to the Sundara Mandiram, the house in which Ramana Maharshi was born, now kept as a quiet place of remembrance and meditation.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most small-town temples of the region. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruchuli is about 15 km east of Aruppukottai and some 45 km south of Madurai by road, on the Virudhunagar–Manamadurai route. The town has a railway station on the Virudhunagar–Manamadurai line; Madurai Airport is the nearest airport.
